name: Czechia
summary_text: Czechia is broadly workable with an improving trajectory and a major welcoming tourist hub (Prague), offset by unprepared detention systems and elevated baseline social hostility. Legal gender recognition no longer requires surgery — the Constitutional Court struck that requirement in 2024 and the Health Ministry implemented reform in 2025 — but it still requires a medical diagnosis and 6–12 months' observation (improving, not self-ID). If detained, the system is unprepared: the Supreme Court in November 2025 demanded prison rules for trans people, and there is a documented case of police mishandling the extradition-detention of an HIV-positive trans foreigner. About half of LGBTIQ people report being targeted by insults, assault or threats over five years, and the far-right SPD uses "deviant" rhetoric; Prague and larger cities are welcoming, but harassment is more likely in rural areas or late at night. Bathrooms are unrestricted, there is no criminalisation of trans identity, and the Schengen border poses no trans-specific friction.

sources.title: Decisions | The Constitutional Court
sources.claim_summary: Czech Constitutional Court judgment PL. US 52/23 (24 April 2024), legal summary: the Court struck down the requirement that surgery including sterilisation be a condition for official legal sex change - a landmark ruling ending compulsory sterilisation for legal gender recognition in Czechia.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying Reuters report (June 2025) covers Czechia dropping the surgery requirement for legal gender change.

sources.title: Policie si neví rady se zajišťováním transgender cizinců, soudy se hašteří - Česká justice
sources.claim_summary: Ceska-justice.cz (March 2023, in Czech): administrative courts clashed over how immigration police handle detained trans foreigners - the Supreme Administrative Court (Judge Baxa panel) criticised the Prague Municipal Court's 'sarcastic moral lectures' toward an HIV-positive trans detainee in transition, and ruled authorities must properly assess whether detainees are 'potentially vulnerable persons' before placement in detention facilities.

sources.title: České věznice nejsou připravené na trans osoby. Soudci kritizují nečinnost vlády - Česká justice
sources.claim_summary: Ceska-justice.cz (Nov 2025, in Czech): Czech prisons are unprepared for trans people and lack clear rules; the Supreme Court demands the prison concept explicitly address the needs of people in or after transition, citing the Constitutional Court ruling that no longer conditions legal gender change on surgery; the human-rights commissioner supports a binding regulation while the ministry claims existing frameworks suffice.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Czechia: politicians' anti-LGBT speech rose from 43% (2018) to 71% (2023); 43% of LGBT+ people reported discrimination/harassment in five years, highest among trans and non-binary respondents; a drag story-time event was disrupted in Brno; the new Asylum Law includes SOGI grounds; Pride Business Forum published a trans-inclusive workplace toolkit.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Czechia: after the Constitutional Court repealed the surgery requirement for legal gender recognition, the Justice Minister made transphobic statements ('to prevent men from giving birth'); the SPD party circulated anti-LGBT election leaflets; the government approved a Criminal Code amendment extending hate-crime protections to sexual orientation and gender identity (pending in Parliament).

sources.title: Safety and security - Czechia travel advice - GOV.UK
sources.claim_summary: UK Foreign travel advice for Czechia: safety and security section (terrorism threat, crime, etc.). General travel advice, not trans-specific.

sources.title: LGBTQ+ safety during solo travel in Czechia - All About Czech
sources.claim_summary: Travel portal (Feb 2026): Prague and larger cities are generally welcoming for LGBTQ+ solo travellers, but harassment can occur and risk is higher in rural areas or late-night settings; practical safety tips and local resources.

OSCE/ODIHR 2024 Hate Crime Report for the Czech Republic: regularly reports data; 94 hate crimes recorded by police in 2024, 46 prosecuted, 42 sentenced; Action Plans on Combating Extremism and Prejudicial Hatred introduced 2023; ODIHR notes recording does not sufficiently distinguish hate crimes.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (timeout); the underlying ECHR document (hudoc 001-243567) relates to a Court of Human Rights judgment concerning Czechia.

sources.title: Manželství místo partnerství. Vláda podpořila sňatky pro homosexuály – Deník.cz
sources.claim_summary: Deník/ČTK (June 2018, in Czech): the Czech government supported a bill allowing same-sex marriage (46 MPs from six parties), which would replace registered partnerships; the Jsme fér ('We Are Fair') campaign welcomed the decision - context of the marriage-equality debate.
